- **Layer smart** — put dense root veggies on the bottom near the heat, meat on top.
- **Brown meat first** — it adds depth of flavor that slow cooking alone won't create.
- **Watch the liquid** — slow cookers trap moisture, so use less liquid than stovetop recipes (about a third less).
- **Add delicate things late** — dairy, herbs, pasta, and quick-cooking veggies go in the last 30 minutes.
- **Boost flavor at the end** — finish with fresh herbs, a splash of vinegar or lemon, or salt to taste.
- **Keep the lid on** — every peek adds 15–20 minutes to cook time.
- **Use the right setting** — "Low" for tougher cuts (8+ hours), "High" for leaner meats and shorter cooks (4–6 hours).

Since you're eyeing that Gibson Les Paul as an upgrade from your Strat, here's what to focus on while you're at the store:

- **Try before you buy** — play several units of the same model; they vary a lot in weight and neck feel (Les Pauls can run heavy, 9+ lbs).
- **Neck & setup** — check action, fret wear, and that it stays in tune, especially since you've been exploring open D tuning.
- **Pickups & tone** — ABR-1 vs. modern wiring, coil-tap options; test clean and overdriven through an amp, not just unplugged.
- **Build quality** — binding, fret ends, tuning machines, and bridge stability.
- **Compare against your Strat** — note how the humbucker warmth and sustain differ from your single coils; that tonal shift is the whole point of the Les Paul.
- **Ask about a setup** — a good store will include a fresh setup; budget for it if not.
- **Bring your picks and play your own material** — a guitar that feels right under your hands beats any spec sheet.

And since you believe music and art can transform the world — pick the one that makes you want to play longer. Enjoy the trip!
